extraFacts.fact: SAE J514 is the standard for 37° flared tube fittings (JIC): the male flare and the female swivel nut seat against each other on a 74° included cone.
extraFacts.source: SAE J514 Hydraulic Tube Fittings, scope; ISO 8434-2 (37° flared fittings)

extraFacts.fact: NPT is a tapered pipe thread standardised in ASME B1.20.1; it seals on the thread with sealant such as PTFE tape or paste.
extraFacts.source: ASME B1.20.1 Pipe Threads, General Purpose (Inch), scope

extraFacts.fact: SAE J1453 covers O-ring face seal (ORFS) fittings: a flat-faced male carries an O-ring in its face and the female swivel nut pulls it against the mating face.
extraFacts.source: SAE J1453 Fitting - O-Ring Face Seal, scope; ISO 8434-3

extraFacts.fact: ISO 228-1 covers parallel (non-taper) pipe threads, the G or BSPP thread; the seal is made by a seat, bonded washer or O-ring at the face, not by the thread flanks.
extraFacts.source: ISO 228-1:2000 Pipe threads where pressure-tight joints are not made on the threads, scope

extraFacts.fact: ASTM B633 specifies electrodeposited zinc coatings on iron and steel; trivalent zinc plating is a chromium-VI-free finish on that coating.
extraFacts.source: ASTM B633 Electrodeposited Coatings of Zinc on Iron and Steel, scope

extraFacts.fact: Zinc plating gives mild corrosion protection but vaporises at the weld, so on a zinc-plated part the coating is cleared from the weld zone and the weld area is ventilated.
extraFacts.source: American Welding Society safety and health fact sheets on welding zinc-coated steel

faqs.q: Which standards apply to the Steel Weld-On Tube × JIC 37° Female Swivel Adapter?
faqs.a: The JIC 37° female swivel end of the Steel Weld-On Tube × JIC 37° Female Swivel Adapter is made to SAE J514: it is a 37° flare seat on a 74° included cone, with a swivel nut that turns freely on the body. faqs.q: What does the Steel Weld-On Tube × JIC 37° Female Swivel Adapter connect to?

faqs.q: How do I weld and fit the Steel Weld-On Tube × JIC 37° Female Swivel Adapter?
faqs.a: Clean the weld end and clear the zinc plating from the weld zone, weld it to the tube or hose with a procedure and filler to suit the base material, and ventilate the area because zinc fume is released. Keep heat and spatter off the 37° flare seat and swivel nut, and re-protect the weld afterwards. Make up the joint to the torque in the [make-up torque guide](/blog/hydraulic-fitting-make-up-torque).
